tasks.title: The server is not listening on a UDP port
tasks.statement: The client sends datagrams to port 5000 of the server but receives nothing. In the client terminal run `nc -u 192.168.0.20 5000` and look at the response: an ICMP “port unreachable” comes back. Start listening on UDP port 5000 on the server and try again.
tasks.hint: In the server terminal: `nc -u -l 5000`. Or in the server card, “Listening ports”: protocol udp, port 5000. A TCP port with the same number is a different socket and will not help.

spec_text./goals/0/text: The client gets a response on UDP port 5000

tasks.title: TCP and UDP on one server
tasks.statement: The server must answer web requests (TCP, port 80) and name queries (UDP, port 53). Right now it listens on nothing. Open both ports and check each one: TCP port 53 must stay closed, because different protocols use different sockets.
tasks.hint: In the server card, “Listening ports” section: choose protocol tcp, port 80; then udp, port 53. Terminal: `nc -l 80` and `nc -u -l 53`.

tasks.title: Firewall: DNS and web only
tasks.statement: The home gateway denies everything by default (policy DROP on FORWARD). NAT is already configured. Open for the network's clients what they need: DNS queries (udp/53) and web (tcp/80), and also allow replies to connections that are already established. SSH (tcp/22) must stay closed.
tasks.hint: FORWARD rules in order: 1) `-m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT` (replies), 2) `-p udp --dport 53 -j ACCEPT`, 3) `-p tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT`. In the firewall form choose the state “already established” for the first rule.

spec_text./goals/0/text: A DNS query (udp/53) gets a response

tasks.title: Refusal or silence
tasks.statement: Two servers must answer over UDP on port 5000. The client tries both. With the first, a reply comes immediately as an ICMP “port unreachable” (a refusal); with the second there is silence (packets vanish). These are two different causes: on the first the port is simply not listening, while on the second something drops packets along the way. Fix both.
tasks.hint: First: open UDP port 5000 on server 1 (`nc -u -l 5000`). Second: on the router, find “firewall: DROP” in the log and delete the rule that blocks UDP to port 5000.
